newsitem.title: USA: BoJ policy aimed at sustaining recovery -- Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: BoJ policy aimed at sustaining recovery -- Mitsuzuka.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday that the monetary policy of the Bank of Japan is geared to sustaining Japan's economic recovery.

In a speech addressed to the interim committee meeting of the International Monetary Fund, Mitsuzuka said the April 1 increase in Japan's consumption tax is likely to slow economic growth temporarily in the first half of the current 1997/98 fiscal year.
The consumption tax was raised to five percent from three percent.
However, the current economic recovery led by domestic demand will likely continue due to improvements in production, corporate profits and people's income, he said.
"As for BOJ's monetary policy, the bank has made it clear that it continues to put emphasis on strengthening the basis of economic recovery," he said.

He repeated his remarks at a meeting on Sunday of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations that Japan's surplus in goods and services trade is unlikely to increase substantially over the medium term.

He also reiterated that currency stability is needed not only for economies in industrial nations but for the world economy. "It is necessary for industrial nations to continue close cooperation in currency markets," he said.

In a statement issued by the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States, top economic policymakers said they opposed wild swings in currency rates and they would monitor the markets to see if their wishes were carried out.
